text: Photography begins with the shutter, which is responsible for opening and closing to allow light to enter the camera. When a fast shutter speed is used, it captures only a brief fraction of the light available, capturing the action. The aperture, which controls the amount of light entering the camera, is larger when shooting in darker settings and smaller when shooting in lighter settings. By adjusting the aperture, the camera can capture more light and use slower shutter speeds, or use faster shutter speeds when a larger aperture is employed.
